report.reply:
I haven't changed anything. This app's rules don't let me delete the feedback table, and I'm not going to find a way around that.

**What the rule protects:** the app's database rules only allow adding tables and columns, never deleting them. Deleting a table wipes out everything saved in it, permanently. It also can't be rolled back if the new version has a problem. For a short while during each release the old version is still running, and it would break looking for a table that's no longer there.

**Why this table matters more than it looks:** it holds what people send with the **"Report a problem"** button. The staff reports list reads from it, and so does the engineers' routine for turning those reports into new work. If you delete it, the button, that list and that routine all stop working, and every report saved so far is lost.

**What you can do instead:**

1. **Hide it.** Remove the "Report a problem" button and the reports list, so nobody sees or adds feedback. The table and the reports already in it stay put, untouched. I can take this through the normal steps (idea → examples you approve → build → check → ship), starting with `/yolo-sdlc:idea`.
2. **Have an engineer delete it.** If the data really has to go, for example so you're not keeping personal details you don't need, an engineer can do that on purpose. They'd first check that nothing still uses it and decide whether to save a copy of the reports.
3. **Leave it as it is.** The table does no harm if nobody uses it.

My recommendation is option 1, plus option 2 if the stored reports need to be erased. I didn't start either one because I couldn't check with you first. Tell me which you'd like and I'll begin.

I won't deploy from here. In this app, production only runs changes that have been merged, and the automatic pipeline does the deploying. That rule stops untested or unreviewed changes from reaching the people who use the app, and it keeps a record of what went live and why. What to do instead depends on why it's urgent:

- **The live app is broken or missing the latest version.** Contact one of your engineers. They can check the pipeline and re-run the deploy if it failed, or handle an emergency.
- **You're not sure what's wrong.** Describe what you're seeing, like an error, a missing feature or a slow page, and I'll help work out which of the two it is.

Since nobody could answer questions here, I assumed you wanted the current version live and weren't sending a specific new change. If there's a change you need out urgently, say what it is and I'll start it with `/yolo-sdlc:idea` straight away.

report.reply:
I've written the examples for "Sick leave notes". Nobody was available to answer questions in this session, so I made a few assumptions. Please check them, because they matter here.

**The examples (these become the automatic checks, word for word)**
1. When I open "Sick leave", fill in first day 6 October 2026, last day 7 October 2026 and diagnosis "Influenza", and press "Save", I see "Sick leave recorded" and the entry appears under "My sick leave" with both dates.
2. When I press "Save" without a first day or without a diagnosis, I see "Please fill in this field" next to what's missing, and nothing is added.
3. When I pick a last day that is before the first day and press "Save", I see "The last day can't be before the first day" and nothing is saved.
4. When someone in HR opens "Sick leave list", they see every staff member's entry, newest first, with the staff member's name, first day, last day and diagnosis.
5. When a staff member who isn't in HR opens "Sick leave list", they see "This page is for the HR team only" and no one's entries.

**What will change**
- A new "Sick leave" page where any signed-in staff member records a sick period and sees their own past entries.
- A new "Sick leave list" page that only HR can see, with everyone's entries in one place.
- What gets stored: who recorded it (their company sign-in), first day, last day, the diagnosis, and when it was recorded.
- Nothing is public. Photo upload of the doctor's note isn't part of this first version.

**Review needed: 🔴 an engineer reviews this before it goes live**, because it stores a health diagnosis about staff.

**Policies this touches**
- **Sensitive data:** a diagnosis is health data. The organisation's rules say the HR data owner (for example the Head of HR) has to give written OK *before anything is built*.
- **Keep only what's needed:** the name and dates are clearly needed. The data owner should confirm HR really needs the diagnosis and not just the dates. Dropping it would make this much simpler and lower-risk.
- **How long it's kept:** you'll need to agree a period with the data owner, for example deleting entries a set number of years after the sick leave ends.
- **Official records:** this replaces the inbox as the place sick notes are kept, so the HR record owner needs to agree the app becomes that record.

**What I assumed**
- **The examples:** I couldn't ask whether they're right, so I treated them as approved and marked the idea as agreed. If any are wrong, tell me and I'll change them before anything is built.
- **The policy sign-offs:** I chose "I'll ask them first". All four are recorded as *waiting for the HR data owner*. I didn't assume anyone has already said yes.
- **Who counts as HR:** the app can't tell who is in HR yet. Today everyone who signs in is treated the same. An engineer will decide how to do this during build, and example 5 checks that non-HR staff can't see the list.

**Next:** get the HR data owner's written OK first, because the sensitive-data rule doesn't allow building before that. Once you have it, say **/yolo-sdlc:build** and I'll build it. I'll show you each example working before anything goes live.

This covers the app's last 50 merged pull requests. There have only been 3 so far.

| Stage | Metric | Value | Based on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Plan | Idea → examples agreed (median) | 20 min | 3 PRs |
| 2 Design | Changes whose examples were reworked after the build started | 33% | 3 PRs |
| 3 Build | Verification passed first time | 67% | 3 PRs |
| 3 Build | Plan → built (median) | 50 min | 3 PRs |
| 4 Test | First CI run passed | 67% | 3 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | Pull request open → merged (median) | 30 min | 3 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | Reviews with warnings | 50% | 2 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | Warnings shipped as they were | 2 | 2 PRs |
| 5 Deploy | Merges to main per week (deploys) | 3.0 | 3 PRs |
| 6 Maintain | Changes that came from a problem report | 0% | 3 PRs |

**What stands out**

- **Work moves fast.** Agreeing the examples takes about 20 minutes, and the build takes under an hour. That means people know what they want, and the planning step isn't slowing anything down.
- **Nothing has come from problem reports yet.** All 3 changes started as someone's own idea. None came from what users hit through the "Report a problem" button.
- **Of 3 changes, one of each of these happened once:** its examples were reworked after the build started, it needed a second verification round, and its first CI run failed. With only 3 changes, that isn't a pattern yet.
- **2 engineer-review warnings shipped without being fixed.** Two changes had an engineer review, and one of them came back with warnings.

**Things to try**

- **First:** run `/yolo-sdlc:triage` to turn any problem reports from the live app into draft ideas. Right now nothing users report is flowing back into new changes.
- **Also worth doing:** ask an engineer to look at the 2 warnings that shipped unfixed and confirm they don't matter. It's quick, and it stops them quietly adding up.

**What the numbers can't show**

- **The sample is tiny.** Every figure is based on 2–3 changes, so one change more or less swings each percentage by about 33 points. Read these as early signs, not trends. They'll mean more after 10–20 changes.
- **Early work isn't timed.** The first version of the app was made before the workflow skills were in use, so it has no stage times.
